hints: Read the medians at cumulative frequency $700$ (50% of 1400) for both Mathematics and English.
Compare the central tendency by stating which subject has the higher median mark.
Read the lower quartiles at cumulative frequency $350$ and upper quartiles at $1050$ to compute the interquartile ranges (or read minimum and maximum to find ranges).
Compare the spread by explicitly contrasting the numerical values of the IQR or range for both subjects.
walkthrough:
Read the medians at cumulative frequency $700$ (half of 1400 pupils):
$$\text{Median for Mathematics} = 40$$
$$\text{Median for English} = 55$$
Comparison of central tendency: English has a higher median mark than Mathematics ($55 > 40$), indicating generally higher achievement in English.

Read the quartiles to measure spread using the interquartile range (IQR):
$$\text{For Mathematics: } Q_1 \approx 20, \; Q_3 \approx 88 \implies \mathrm{IQR} = 88 - 20 = 68$$
$$\text{For English: } Q_1 \approx 45, \; Q_3 \approx 65 \implies \mathrm{IQR} = 65 - 45 = 20$$
Alternatively, using the overall ranges:
$$\text{Range for Mathematics} = 100 - 0 = 100$$
$$\text{Range for English} = 85 - 25 = 60$$
Comparison of spread: Mathematics marks show a much greater spread than English marks ($68 > 20$ for IQR, or $100 > 60$ for range), showing higher variability in Mathematics performance.

teacher_walkthrough: We need to compare the central tendency and spread of marks between Mathematics and English using the cumulative frequency curves for 1400 pupils.

Step 1: Find the median for each subject.
The total number of pupils is $N = 1400$. The median corresponds to the cumulative frequency of:
$$\frac{1400}{2} = 700$$
- Drawing a horizontal line at 700 to the Mathematics curve gives $\text{Median} = 40$.
- Drawing a horizontal line at 700 to the English curve gives $\text{Median} = 55$.

Step 2: Compare central tendency in context:
English has a higher median mark than Mathematics ($55$ compared to $40$). This shows that the average performance of pupils was higher in English.

Step 3: Measure the spread using the Interquartile Range (IQR).
- Lower quartile ($Q_1$) is at cumulative frequency $0.25 \times 1400 = 350$:
  Mathematics: $Q_1 \approx 20$
  English: $Q_1 \approx 45$
- Upper quartile ($Q_3$) is at cumulative frequency $0.75 \times 1400 = 1050$:
  Mathematics: $Q_3 \approx 88$
  English: $Q_3 \approx 65$
- Calculate the IQRs:
  $$\mathrm{IQR}_{\text{Math}} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 88 - 20 = 68$$
  $$\mathrm{IQR}_{\text{English}} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 65 - 45 = 20$$

Step 4: Compare spread in context:
Mathematics has a much larger interquartile range than English ($68$ compared to $20$). Mathematics marks are far more widely dispersed and varied, while English marks are closely clustered around the median.
